correctness.rationale: For k,m>=2 and any nonzero nonnegative k-periodic multigrain pattern, the synchronous integer firing recurrence c_j(t+1)=c_j(t)-1_{c_j(t)>0}+1_{c_(j-1)(t)>0} preserves each residue fiber exactly. Thus each lifted firing set is the full inverse image of a base firing set, including every transient stage. Each face of the lifted simplicial complex is precisely a subset whose support projects to a base face. Sum barycentric coordinates over each fiber (Pi) and distribute evenly within fibers (J); Pi J=id, J Pi is the rotation fixed-locus projection, and segment homotopy (1-s)x+s JPi(x) remains in a common full lifted simplex. The rotation-equivariant strong deformation retraction is filtration-compatible, so integral persistence and triviality of rotation action follow. The b=(0,1,...,1) sphere and b=(1,0,...,0) disconnected conclusions follow from full boundary/singleton firing-set families. Independently simulated 5,130 exact recurrence state checks over k=2..4, m=2..4 and b_i=0,1,2 (nonzero), agreeing with fiber projection. This finite check supplements, not replaces, the universal homotopy proof.

originality.rationale: PASS qualified. Riihimäki and Smith (2026) define the avalanche filtration and conjecture a residue-class sphere, but the full reviewed text does not assert arbitrary multigrain periodic-lift rotation-fixed filtration deformation retracts. The published coprime residue theorem concerns n=kq+s with 1<=s<k and gcd(s,k)=1, excluding exactly n=mk, and provides non-equivariant ordinary homotopy types, not the new all-t strong retraction. Abstract simplicial fiber-inflation contraction is standard and earns no novelty credit by itself; the natural sandpile-dynamic realization, universal multigrain and persistence compatibility form the remaining distinction. Historical equivalent covering-space formulations remain an O risk.

value.rationale: PASS. The dynamic repetition parameter naturally asks whether avalanche homology or persistence depends on the number of copies, especially around the published residue-zero sphere prediction. Establishing a full filtered equivariant answer for every multigrain pattern is a structural reduction, not a gratuitous relabeling: it changes the simplicial vertex count by a factor m while preserving canonical persistent homology. A researcher can use the exact reduction to compute lifted systems through a much smaller base. It does not solve nonperiodic or non-cycle cases.
